question: Should OpenClaw permanently admit exact-ID `workspace-directory` Codex plugins that are already installed and enabled, while relying on the upstream plugin RPC contract that Codex currently documents as under development?
rationale: The implementation and proof support the proposed controls, but accepting account-scoped plugin tools and the unstable upstream dependency is a product and security commitment that code review cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve constrained boundary
options.body: Accept workspace plugins only with exact marketplace-qualified IDs, installed/enabled state, proven app ownership and accessibility, default denial, no installation, and an explicit compatible-app-server requirement.

options.title: Defer workspace support
options.body: Keep curated-only behavior until the upstream plugin API is production-supported or maintainers choose a different permanent boundary.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained boundary
recommendation.body: Accept workspace plugins only with exact marketplace-qualified IDs, installed/enabled state, proven app ownership and accessibility, default denial, no installation, and an explicit compatible-app-server requirement.
